recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Name: Gabe (Slick Dissident)
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Role: Co-host of Vibe Rant; teacher of occult symbolism & tarot

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "An Extended Flow State of Art and Reading", "body": "Chance opened the evening as a special extended edition of Vibe Rant, joined by Gabe, Rachel and newcomer Martin. He explained that Flow State meant reading to each other, reflecting on the text and making art on screen, and he urged listeners at home to grab a pencil or canvas and create along with the show. Chance said the format was inspired by Jim Maiden and S.B. Alger, whose older show worked the same way. People shared art all night, from a spider and web T-shirt design to Chance's older marker drawings."}, {"title": "Secret Societies, Mechanism, and Mysticism", "body": "Gabe described his new video series on a rough history of secret societies, which ran fifty minutes, his longest yet. He color coded Gnostics in red and Hermetics in purple, equating science with the Hermetics, and argued that the groups blended around the Industrial Revolution and the World Wars. Chance said his intention was to demystify occult material, and he cited Wilhelm Reich's Ether, God and Devil, saying the mechanistic and the mystic were two imbalanced sides of one way of thinking. The conversation settled on the idea that higher realms might exist while this world could still be understood as heaven."}, {"title": "German New Medicine, Jung, and Dreams", "body": "Rachel read the introduction and first chapter of a book on German New Medicine, a framework that mainstream medicine does not accept. Afterward one participant questioned the book's tie between energy medicine and quantum physics but liked the idea that the brain rings echoed the concentric layers of the biofield, and another speaker said the premise matched how emotional experience showed up in the body. Kayleigh read from Carl Jung's Man and His Symbols, and later a guest read Jung on dreams, free association and the anima. The text argued that a dream should be examined as it appears, and one participant said Jung offered useful tools for shadow work."}, {"title": "Zanoni, Hermetic Call Signs, and Second Sight", "body": "A guest read the preface and introduction to Zanoni by Bulwer-Lytton, and participants then hunted for codes. The six Rosicrucian precepts were read aloud, and Gabe argued that HG, GH, pH and HP were call signs of Hermes and pointed to the twin pH's in Philadelphia. S.B. read from a printed Treatise on Second Sight, whose preface proposed that mountain apparitions came from atmospheric refraction, as with the specter of the Brocken. S.B. also described sensing that a friend was delayed on his way to a gathering, and another participant described a vivid visionary experience."}, {"title": "Superstition, Lincoln's Cabin, and Serpents", "body": "Early in the night a reader took the room through verses of the Havamal about lies and love, and later participants argued that old superstitions might have rested on real energetic knowledge. Chance read an article saying the Lincoln birthplace cabin was assembled decades after his death and moved between expositions. He argued that the name Abraham encoded the highest father of darkness, and participants traded theories about the Pinkertons and the assassination. A guest read Odin verses urging people to be only a little wise, and Gabe argued that the boot heel of Italy crushed the serpent's head. Chance later said he quit numbering his main show."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Tonight's Vibe Rant is going down Flow State style, where everyone is invited to come on screen, show us their art process, and take turns reading from books or articles of their choosing.
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "The goal is that you at home go get a pencil and a pen or a piece of paper or a canvas if you fancy. Do some kind of creative flow while you're listening to this and engage the left brain, right brain.
